topic.title: Flow Matching and Efficient Probability Transport
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: Flow-based generators learn how to move a simple distribution toward data through a continuous vector field. This topic studies the choice of paths, couplings, conditioning, and objectives that make that transport easier to learn and sample. Straighter or less ambiguous trajectories can reduce the number of evaluations needed for generation.
topic.whyItMatters: A mathematically valid path can still be inefficient numerically. Choosing how noise and examples are paired affects gradient variance, transport cost, and the speed–quality tradeoff of the resulting sampler.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives include probability-flow learning and continuous-time density models. Recent flow-matching work uses minibatch couplings, energy formulations, and learned forward processes. The newest examples add history and spatial context to shortcut flows, while other studies examine transport variants and membership signals along interpolation paths.
openQuestions: Which path properties predict low-step sample quality before full training?
How can efficient transport retain diversity without exposing additional memorization signals?
